A [virtual private network or VPN](https://www.techtarget.com/searchnetworking/definition/virtual-private-network) is essential for companies who want to provide secure, reliable access to their network for employees. Unfortunately, VPNs are a classic example of a solution to one problem that creates others. VPN connections can be difficult to set up and troubleshoot in hybrid and multicloud applications, particularly in sprawling enterprise networks.

Aviatrix’s newest offering, the [Aviatrix Secure Network Supervisor Agent](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/03/24/microsoft-unveils-microsoft-security-copilot-agents-and-new-protections-for-ai/), uses the power of AI and an integration with Microsoft Copilot for Security to simplify and secure VPN connections. Learn how this integration streamlines management while restoring full control to networking teams.

## VPNs: A Security Solution That Creates New Challenges

VPNs are popular with enterprise companies because they protect sensitive data and provide user anonymity. However, VPNs bring problems of their own. IT departments may frequently find themselves trying to troubleshoot VPNs across time zones and locations.

### Operational Friction and Delays

Slow connections, lost passwords, certificate errors, firewall interference, and other potential issues can cause VPN downtimes that prevent employees from logging into systems or easily accessing data they need, slowing down your entire company’s productivity. Troubleshooting VPN issues becomes a significant operational burden.

### Security Blind Spots and Risk of Data Breaches

When the issue is misconfigured VPN tunnels, the result can be a security threat to your whole network. Unpatched VPN Software or Split Tunneling misconfigurations allow for unencrypted traffic to bypass security controls, creating significant [security breaches](https://dispersive.io/blog/vpns-under-siege-2024-cyber-attacks-data-breach-in-review) that put customer data and risk and can result in millions of dollars in penalties.

## Aviatrix Secure Network Supervisor Agent: AI Intelligence for Fine-Tuned Control

The Aviatrix Secure Network Supervisor resolves complex VPN challenges by monitoring specific VPN connections for errors and misconfigurations, then uses GenAI to speed up the troubleshooting and remediation process. You can easily enable the agent through Aviatrix CoPolit and choose the level of autonomy you want it to have: simple alerts, resetting connections when they’re down, or requesting user input to run advanced troubleshooting flows using [Aviatrix FlightPath](https://docs.aviatrix.com/documentation/latest/platform-administration/controller/flightpath.html?expand=true).

When you set up the agent to run advanced troubleshooting, the agent will reference user input against a trained large language model (LLM) that has incorporated the health data from a specific connection, along with any relevant log messages.

## Holistic, Unified Control

Aviatrix’s Secure Network Supervisor Agent combines our comprehensive cloud security fabric with Microsoft Security Copilot’s generative AI platform to offer unified control, visibility, and automation across clouds. This integrated solution provides:

- **The first and only network security-focused Copilot agent** purpose-built to analyze the root causes of VPN issues

- **Deep visibility** through real-time network telemetry from Aviatrix’s Cloud Firewall platform

- **Defense-in-depth** by connecting infrastructure-level insights with SOC workflows

- Alignment with **Microsoft’s AI-driven SecOps vision**


Don’t wait for the next VPN failure to bring business to a halt. Activate AI-assisted remediation now—before downtime and data loss become tomorrow’s headlines. The Aviatrix Secure Network Supervisor Agent is now ready in Private Preview. To learn more, [schedule a demo](https://aviatrix.ai/get-started/) or reach out to [sales@aviatrix.com](mailto:sales@aviatrix.com).
